org.diylc.appframework.update.Change.description: Upgrade Java version to 21
Fixed scaling for 'Image' and 'SVG Image' components; it was showing as unrecognized
Fixed errors while analyzing guitar wiring diagrams caused by treble bleed enhancements
Improved handling of larger AI analysis requests and added more token budget per request to Supporter and Pro plans
Files containing Inductor Symbol fail to open
Added two new view perspectives to Potentiometer component - Terminals Up and Terminals down
Use either username of email to log into DIYLC cloud
Improved comparison logic of the 'Compare With..' tool
Align Potentiometer 1-2-3 markings with circuit analysis node labels; it used to be mixed up in some cases
Added support for stacked guitar pickups: 'Stacked - North' and 'Stacked - South' are two new options to pick in the Coil(s) property of Single Coil, P-90, P-Bass and Jazz Bass pickups
Added 'Node Name Tooltips' feature that can be toggled in the Config menu; when enabled a tooltip is shown next to the cursor with names of component nodes under the cursor
Significantly improved AI Assistant's knowledge base on DIYLC usage by ingesting most of the material from the eBook
Improved the accuracy of board underside rendering; some of the components were not rendered in the right place or at all
Show a progress dialog while waiting for a long-running AI Analysis to complete
Renamed Mac OS build files to start with a 'mac' prefix instead of 'osx'
Images can randomly disappear when zooming in and scrolling

Building blocks instantiate by default as a single component, inheriting control points and terminal nodes from all individual components but acting as a single component; still possible to instantiate individual components using 'Insert as Grouped Components' action from the context menu over a building block

Added ability to set node name (or names) for some connectivity components (e.g. Solder Pad, Eyelet, PCB Terminal Block, etc); when combined into building blocks, these names will become node names of the composite component stamped from the building block
Include building blocks in the Recently Used category
When saving building blocks, present a drop down list with most recently used building blocks for quick selection
Prompt to confirm the overwrite when saving over the existing building blocks
When transistor pinout is selected for TO-1, TO-92, TO-126, TO-220 transistor, the corresponding electrode name will be used as a node name in programmatical and AI analysis
Diode components now label their terminal nodes as 'A' (anode) and 'K' (cathode) instead of '1' and '2'
Capacitor components now label their terminal nodes as '+' and '-' instead of '1' and '2' when 'Polarized' property is ticked
Percentage values such as transparency Alpha, image Scale, etc, can have decimal values and not just integers
Made announcement bubbles and dialogs that contain links clickable
Arduino Mega 2560
Arduino Nano - ATmega328, 33 BLE, 33 BLE Sense, 33 IoT, ESP32, Every, R4, RP3040 Connect
Arduino Uno - R3, R4 Minima, R4 WiFi, Leonardo
ESP32 - DevKit V1 (30-pin), DevKitC V4 (38-pin), S3 DevKitC-1 (44-pin), C3 DevKitM-1 (30-pin), C6 DevKitC-1 (32-pin)
ESP8266 NodeMCU
Raspberry Pi - 3B+, 4B, 5
Raspberry Pi - Pico, Pico W, Pico 2, Pico 2 W
Raspberry Pi - Zero, Zero 2, Zero 2 W
WeMos D1 Mini
Upgraded AI models to faster and smarter versions across all tiers, especially Supporter and Pro
Added 'Right Angle Wire' and 'Right Angle Line' components that route between two points using only horizontal and vertical runs with rounded corners
Double click on a component type in the tree or the toolbar to instantiate it at once, even for those that are intended to be placed point-by-point
All curved components ('Curved Trace', 'Hookup Wire', 'Twisted Leads') are now getting created between the two points by default instead of getting created with some preset shape and length
Improve terminal node naming within building blocks to ensure no duplicates by adding a name of the nested component as a prefix
7-Segment Display - 1-digit 0.56 inch, 2-digit 0.56 inch, 4-digit in 0.36 inch and 0.56 inch, and TM1637 driver module
Character LCD - 16x2 and 20x4, with I2C backpack or 16-pin parallel interface
LED Bar Graph - 4, 5, 6, 8, 10 and 12 segments
LED Matrix (MAX7219) - single 8x8, compact 8x8, 4-in-1 32x8, 8-in-1 64x8
NeoPixel Breakout (WS2812B) - single LED
NeoPixel Jewel (WS2812B) - 7 LEDs
NeoPixel Panel (WS2812B) - 8x8, 64 LEDs
NeoPixel Ring (WS2812B) - 12, 16 and 24 LEDs
NeoPixel Stick (WS2812B) - 8 LEDs
NeoPixel Strip (WS2812B) - 30, 60 and 144 LEDs per meter, up to 144 LEDs
Nokia 5110 LCD (PCD8544)
OLED Display - 0.96 inch SSD1306, 0.91 inch SSD1306, 1.3 inch SH1106, in I2C, 7-pin SPI and 6-pin SPI
TFT Display - 2.8 inch and 2.4 inch ILI9341, 1.8 inch and 0.96 inch ST7735, 1.54 inch ST7789, 1.28 inch round GC9A01
Added ability to hide component categories in the component tree and toolbar from the Config menu
Bill of Materials now lists the selected variant of microcontroller boards and displays, so different versions of the same board are no longer merged into a single row
4-pin Jumbo Tube Socket - the two filament pins are now labeled F1 and F2 instead of both being labeled F, so they no longer read as the same node
Netlists now treat the repeated supply pins of a microcontroller or display board as one node, so grounding a single GND pin no longer leaves the others floating

Added 'Align & Distribute' to the Edit menu and the right-click menu - align the selected components by their left, right, top or bottom edges or their centers, or space them evenly by their centers or by the gaps between them

Holding 'Shift' when starting to drag components or control points keeps the whole drag strictly horizontal or vertical, in the direction of the initial gesture. Holding 'Shift' while drawing a new wire or two-point component does the same
Added Rectangular shape to LED component in addition to Round; added ability to set LED lead spacing
Upgraded AI Models to the latest GPT-6 generation across all tiers
'S1 Switch' can now be rotated to match the orientation of the potentiometer it is mounted on, so the switching matrix stays correct relative to the pot lugs
'Cut Line' can be rotated using keyboard shortcuts
Include 'Potentiometer (Miniature)' and 'Trimmer Potentiometer' in Guitar Wiring Analyzer
Significantly improved rendering performance and reduced lagging with complex projects while dragging components around
Improved performance of application initialization
Improved performance of 'Project Explorer' pane
Improved memory management when caching rendered components
Improved grid rendering on screen and when exporting; PDF export of the grid is now vector-based and does not get blurry on zooming in
Updated localization files with translations for recently added UI elements and messages
Fixed the issue of disappearing components in some edge cases

Fixed netlists and 'Highlight Connected Areas' giving inconsistent results on boards with trace cuts - running them again could join strips across a cut, and a moved or deleted cut could leave the strip broken where it used to be

'Twisted Leads' - the last few crossings near the end of a wire were drawn with the leads overlapping instead of one passing over the other, and crossings could come out slightly different between redraws
When a component that belongs to a group is stuck to another component, moving that other component now drags the whole group along instead of only the stuck component
AI Assistant can actively participate in circuit design, make changes to the project and designs circuits from scratch
Added 6PDT and 6PDT On/Off/On toggle switch types

Rotating and mirroring the selection with 'Sticky Points' enabled now keeps the circuit connected, the same way moving it does - wires and leads stuck to the selection stay attached to their pins, and other rigid components stuck to it are rotated or mirrored along with it
Allow active position selection for 'Rotary Switch Sealed', 'DIP Switch', 'Latching Switch Symbol', 'LP Switch', 'S1 Switch', allowing for more accurate circuit analysis and debugging

'Cliff 1/4" Jack' and 'Cliff 1/8" Jack' lugs are now correctly labeled as Tip, Sleeve, Ring and their switched contacts instead of plain numbers, so netlists show what each lug does and 'Analyze Guitar Diagrams' can find the output jack
'Fuse Holder (Panel)' with 'Fuse' turned on now connects its two lugs in the netlist, so a circuit running through the fuse is no longer reported as open
'9V Battery Snap' now has separate + and - terminals, so hookup wires can be connected to each lead and the netlist tells the battery's positive and negative sides apart

'IEC Socket', 'Plastic DC Jack', 'Multi-Section Capacitor' and 'Mini Relay' terminals are now labeled by function (Earth, Line, Neutral; Sleeve, Switch, Center; the shared negative and each section's positive; coil, COM, NC and NO) instead of plain numbers, so netlists show what each terminal does
Improved quality of output from the 'AI Circuit Analyzer'
'AI Circuit Analyzer' offers to log in instead of just showing the error
'AI Assistant' is now aware of what is selected so natural language prompts can refer to selected components
Improved sorting of switching combinations in 'Analyze Guitar Diagrams' tool
Single coil pickups rotated by 90 or 270 degrees had their start and finish lugs swapped relative to the pickup body

'Analyze Guitar Diagrams' ignored 'Stingray Bass Pickup', so a diagram built around it was reported as having no pickups connected to the output jack, and its coils were left out of the hum-cancelling and phase checks
Fixed 'Analyze Guitar Diagrams' logic that merges switching configuration that produce the same outcome; in some cases it would remove switches from the list when it shouldn't

Gerber export on computers set to a language that uses a decimal comma (e.g. German, French, Serbian) produced files in which drill holes, pads and traces had the wrong size - a 0.8mm hole came out as 0mm and traces and the board outline had no width, so the files could not be used for fabrication
Zooming out until the drawing is smaller than the window made the toolbar above the canvas grow taller and squeeze the canvas; the toolbar now keeps its height at every zoom level
Fixed a bug that makes it impossible to clear a property with dynamic values, e.g. 'Selected Position' of a switch
Fixed a bug that makes 'Selected Position' list sometimes shows wrong values
Added 'Pin Names' property to 'DIP IC', 'SIP IC' and 'Multiwatt IC' to name each pin, e.g. 1OUT, 1IN-, VCC+; the names are drawn on the component and used in node tooltips, netlists and AI analysis
Added 'Pin Labels' property to 'SIP IC' and 'Multiwatt IC' to show pin names or pin numbers next to the pins

Added datasheets to 'DIP IC', 'SIP IC' and 'Multiwatt IC' - pick a part by its number from the component's submenu to set its pin count, spacing and pin names at once - more than 100 chips in total; the AI Assistant can place these parts by part number too

Added datasheets to 'Transistor (TO-92)', 'Transistor (TO-1)', 'Transistor (TO-126)', 'Transistor (TO-220)' and 'Transistor (TO-3)' - pick a part by its number from the component's submenu to set its value and pinout at once - more than 250 transistors, JFETs, MOSFETs and voltage regulators used in guitar effects, hi-fi, radio and synth projects; the AI Assistant can place these parts by part number too
Added 'Pinout' property to 'Transistor (TO-3)' and a terminal in the mounting hole next to the pins, so the case (collector) can be wired and shows up in netlists and AI analysis

Added a datasheet to 'Tube Socket' - pick a tube by its type from the component's submenu to set its base and electrode labels at once - more than 180 preamp, power, rectifier, radio, space-charge and Soviet tubes; the AI Assistant can place these tubes by type too
Added the UX4 base to 'Tube Socket', with the 300B, 2A3, 6A3 and 45 triodes and the 5Z3 rectifier in its datasheet

Added datasheets to 'Diode (plastic)' and 'Diode (glass)' - pick a part by its number from the component's submenu to draw it at its real package size and colours - more than 300 rectifiers, Schottky, signal, germanium and zener diodes, including the Japanese clippers of classic overdrive pedals; the AI Assistant can place these parts by part number too

Added 'Pin Names', 'Pin Labels' and 'Thickness' to 'Sub-Mini Tube' to name each lead and draw flat bulbs, and a datasheet with popular Western and Soviet sub-miniature tubes such as 6021, 6111, 5840, 5672, 6N16B and 6N17B that sets leads, bulb size and lead names at once
'Chassis Panel' is now 'Enclosure' and can draw an exploded view of the whole box; set 'Height' and choose which 'Sides' to unfold
Added a datasheet to 'Enclosure' with Hammond 1590, 1550, 1441 and 1444 enclosures and the 125B size - more than 130 variations

Datasheet models in a component's drop-down menu now have the same pin as saved variants, so a model such as a 2N3904 can be made the default that is placed when the component is clicked; a component has one default, so pinning a model replaces a pinned variant and the other way round
Re-modeled factory variants of 'Resistor' and 'Heat Sink Resistor' component types as datasheets in order to make them available to the AI; this will produce more accurate AI-driven edits
Derive the z-order of a building blocks placed as a single component based on its child components
Moved 'Enclosure', cutouts, 'Drill Hole' and 'Dial Scale' to the new 'Hardware' category

Pins of transistors, 'SIP IC', 'DIP Switch' and 'Bridge Rectifier' are now drawn on top of the body, so they stay visible whatever the body transparency, and pins are drawn in the same color on every component, including 'DIP IC', 'Bridge Rectifier', 'LED Bar Graph', trimmers and PCB-mounted 'Tube Socket'
'Electrode Labels' of 'Tube Socket' is now called 'Pin Names', as on ICs, and the new 'Pin Labels' property shows pin names, pin numbers or nothing
Added B-E-C, C-E-B and S-D-G transistor pinouts and ADJ-IN-OUT, IN-OUT-GND and IN-OUT-ADJ regulator pinouts

The '+N' variant count next to a component in the component tree is now a button - click it to pick one of the component's variants or datasheet parts from a drop-down menu, without having to right-click the component
'Transistor (TO-1)' now shows the tab on the rim of the metal can next to pin 1, as on the real part, so the orientation is easy to tell at a glance; turn it off with the new 'Flange' property
'DIP IC' with 'Display Pin #s' set to 'No' numbered its pins in the wrong order in netlists and AI analysis, e.g. pin 8 of an 8-pin IC was reported as pin 5
'Multiwatt IC' numbered its pins row by row instead of alternating between the two rows as on the real package
'Multiwatt IC' in the Multiwatt 11 package had its leads 1.27mm apart instead of 1.7mm; existing Multiwatt 11 parts change shape when the project is opened
'SIP IC' body was drawn too short when 'Pin Spacing' is not a multiple of 0.1 inch, leaving the last pin outside the body
SPICE netlists listed the pins of transistors with E-C-B pinout in the wrong order

'Tube Socket' variants with electrode labels connected pins that share a label in netlists and AI analysis, e.g. both anodes of a 12AX7 or both heater ends; these variants are replaced by the datasheet
'Tube Socket' with a Noval, 7-pin or Duodecar base on a chassis mount did not rotate its mounting notches with the pins when 'Angle' was changed
'Sub-Mini Tube' with circular leads numbered the body centre as lead 1 in netlists and AI analysis, so every real lead was reported one number too high

Added 'Value Notation' to the Config menu to show resistance, capacitance, inductance and voltage values in RKM notation, e.g. 4K7, 0R22, 2n2, 4u7 or 6V3, instead of decimal; values can be typed in either notation, and typing the unit together with the value, e.g. 4K7 or 2.2nF, sets the unit at the same time

The bottom of a board can now be designed directly in its Underside Display, seen the way it will be soldered: components and copper can be selected, moved and stretched there just like on the board itself, new parts placed there or dragged in from the toolbox or the component tree go on the bottom of the board, and hovering over a control point shows its node name. Solder-side work no longer has to be done blind in the see-through top view

Added 'Fade Copper Under Board' to the Config menu, on by default, which controls the see-through look of copper on the bottom of the board on the canvas and in the layout export, PDF and print; turning it off brings back the old look with all copper drawn solid

Resistors, capacitors, diodes, ICs, transistors, switches, jacks, tube sockets and other PCB parts have a new 'Board Side' property to place them on the bottom of the board; bottom parts are drawn faded on the canvas and solid in the board's Underside Display, and Gerber export puts their silkscreen on the bottom layer with the text mirrored, and the silkscreen print-out has a separate page for the bottom; a 'Dot' used as a solder joint can be put on the bottom as well

Boards are now drawn the way they really are, so it is clear at a glance which side you are looking at: the main view shows the component side, with strips, pads, traces and other copper on the bottom of the board showing through it faded, and the Underside Display shows the solder side, with the copper solid and the parts mounted on top faded behind the board. Holes and trace cuts go through the board and stay clear from both sides
Turning a board's 'Underside Transparency' off now draws its Underside Display fully solid, and turning it on fades only the parts on the far side of the board instead of the whole display
Inner layers 1 to 6 are no longer offered for traces, pads and other copper, since boards are two-sided; projects that use them still open unchanged
The 'Layer' property of traces, curved traces, ground fills, solder pads and PCB text is now called 'Board Side', the same as on resistors, ICs and other parts
Rotated labels in pasted components and building blocks were drawn in the wrong place and at the wrong angle while following the mouse, until the components were placed

Projects with a resistor, capacitor or other leaded component whose Width or Length had been cleared in the property editor could not be opened; such values now fall back to the default size, and Width and Length can no longer be left empty

'Highlight Connected Areas', netlists and AI analysis could ignore trace cuts after the board under them was moved or edited, or when the cuts were scrolled out of view, and showed the whole strip as connected
'Solder Pad' on the top layer put its solder mask opening on the bottom layer in Gerber export
Opening an older project with a perfboard or another board warned that the file references unknown component properties
